Eplerenone, as an aldosterone antagonist, is included in the class of drugs that inhibit aldosterone action, and Spironolactone, a known aldosterone antagonist, binds to Nr3c2. This binding likely occurs through a shared mechanism, where the structural similarity between Eplerenone and Spironolactone facilitates their interaction with the same target, Nr3c2. The lowest common ancestor of Eplerenone and Spironolactone, which is the lactone group, may play a role in this interaction, suggesting a common pharmacological pathway. The evidence supports a possible functional link between Eplerenone and Nr3c2, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
